'''Rosalind G. Brewer''' (born 1962) is an American businesswoman and former CEO of [[Walgreens Boots Alliance]], before stepping down in September 2023.<ref name="Kavilanz">{{Cite web |last=Kavilanz |first=Parija |date=September 1, 2023 |title=Walgreens CEO steps down {{!}} CNN Business |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/01/business/walgreens-ceo-steps-down/index.html |access-date=September 4, 2023 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> Brewer is the first woman to become CEO of [[Walgreens Boots Alliance]], group president and COO of [[Starbucks]], and CEO of [[Sam's Club]].<ref name="usat">{{cite news|last1=Durbin|first1=Dee-Ann|title=Walgreens taps Starbucks exec Brewer as its new CEO, becoming the only Black woman leading a Fortune 500 company|work=USA Today|publisher=|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/business/2021/01/27/black-woman-ceo-walgreens-taps-starbucks-exec-roz-brewer-role/4278423001/}}</ref> She  served as the interim president of [[Spelman College]], and as a member of the [[President's Export Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=President's Office {{!}} Spelman College {{!}} Atlanta, GA |url=https://www.spelman.edu/leadership/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250602000212/https://www.spelman.edu/leadership/index.html |archive-date=2025-06-02 |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=www.spelman.edu |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=President's Export Council Members |url=https://www.trade.gov/presidents-export-council-members#:~:text=The%20President's%20Export%20Council%20(PEC)%20advises%20the%20President%20of%20government,%2C%20labor%2C%20and%20government%20sectors. |access-date=March 8, 2024 |website=International Trade Administration}}</ref>

''[[USA Today]]'' referred to her as "one of corporate America's most prominent women and black female executives."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Guynn|first=Jessica|title=Amazon names black Starbucks exec Rosalind Brewer to all-white board in 'barrier-breaking' appointment|work=USA Today|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2019/02/04/amazon-names-starbucks-exec-rosalind-brewer-first-black-board-member/2769779002/}}</ref> Brewer has been called a "Highly Powerful Woman" by ''[[Forbes]]'' and ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'' magazines.

==Early life and education==
Rosalind Brewer was born in 1962 in [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Ernst|first=Alina|title=Rosalind G. Brewer|date=July 7, 2018 |url=https://www.blackpast.org/african-american-history/brewer-rosalind-g-1962/}}</ref> the youngest of five children; they were the first generation in her family to attend college.<ref name=":1" /> Due to her inclination for math and science, Brewer was interested in pursuing a career as a [[physician]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Staff|first=A. Y.|date=September 2, 2012|title=From chemist to CEO, Rosalind Brewer|url=https://www.aymag.com/from-chemist-to-ceo-rosalind-brewer/|access-date=March 24, 2021|website=AY Magazine|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 1980, upon graduating from [[Cass Technical High School]] in Detroit, Brewer enrolled at [[Spelman College]] in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] where she completed her bachelor's degree in chemistry.<ref name="profile">{{cite web|title=Rosalind Brewer|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/rosalind-brewer/|access-date=July 11, 2017|website=Forbes.com}}</ref><ref name="walmart">{{cite web|title=Rosalind G. Brewer- Archived copy|url=http://corporate.walmart.com/our-story/leadership/executive-management/rosalind-brewer|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121101014041/http://corporate.walmart.com/our-story/leadership/executive-management/rosalind-brewer|archive-date=November 1, 2012|access-date=November 12, 2012}}</ref> She decided not to pursue a career in medicine, and began working at [[Kimberly-Clark]] as a research technician.

Brewer completed the director's college (executive education) program at the [[University of Chicago Booth School of Business]] and [[Stanford Law School]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ernst |first=Alina |date=July 7, 2018 |title=Rosalind G. Brewer (1962- ) • |url=https://www.blackpast.org/african-american-history/brewer-rosalind-g-1962/ |access-date=February 7, 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref> as well as the advanced management program at The [[Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Trustee Rosalind G. Brewer, C'84 Spelman College|url=https://www.spelman.edu/about-us/office-of-the-president/board-of-trustees/rosalind-brewer|access-date=March 24, 2021|website=www.spelman.edu}}</ref>

==Career==

Brewer has held executive positions at [[Kimberly-Clark]], [[Walmart]], [[Sam's Club]], [[Starbucks]], and [[Walgreens Boots Alliance]]. Additionally, in 2019 Brewer was elected and became the only black member of the board of directors at Amazon.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|title=Amazon names Starbucks COO Rosalind Brewer to board of directors|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/04/tech/amazon-rosalind-brewer-board|website=CNN Business|date=February 5, 2019 }}</ref> She has been a non-executive director at [[Lockheed Martin]] and [[Molson Coors Brewing Company]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":10">{{Cite news|last=Campbell|first=Megan|title=Starbucks COO Rosalind Brewer to leave for CEO role at Walgreens|work=The Business Journals|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/bizwomen/news/latest-news/2021/01/starbucks-coo-rosalind-brewer-leaves-coffee-giant.html?page=all}}</ref> Brewer continues to serve as a member on the board of trustees for Westminster School, the board of councilors for the Carter Presidential Center, and board of trustees chair at Spelman College.<ref name=":2" /> in 2024 she became a limited partner in the Atlanta Falcons ownership group.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parker |first=Ellie |date=2024-06-05 |title=Falcons add film producer, Olympic gold medalist, 2 others to ownership group |url=https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2024/06/05/falcons-add-film-producer-olympic-gold-medalist-2-others-ownership-group/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=www.atlantanewsfirst.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Kimberly-Clark (1984-2006) ===
In 1984, after graduating from [[Spelman College]], Brewer began her career as a research technician at Kimberly-Clark, a global paper-based product company, till 1988.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|title=How Did I Get Here? Rosalind Brewer|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/features/2016-how-did-i-get-here/rosalind-brewer.html|newspaper=Bloomberg}}</ref> From 1988 to 1998, she held numerous leadership roles including market manager, and director for Skincare.<ref name=":4" /> Between 1998 and 2006, Brewer served as the vice president of Kimberly-Clark's Nonwovens division.<ref name=":4" /> Brewer had a 22-year career at [[Kimberly-Clark Corporation]].<ref name="profile" /><ref name="walmart" />

=== Walmart and Sam's Club (2006-2017) ===
Brewer's career with [[Walmart]] began in 2006. Brewer served as the vice president, senior vice president, executive vice president for southeastern operations, and executive vice president for the eastern business unit at Walmart stores.<ref name=":4" /> Brewer started her position as regional vice president of operations in Georgia. Following her work as the regional vice president of Operations in Georgia, she became the division president of Walmart's southeast market, and finally the president of Walmart East.<ref name="sams-club">{{cite web|title=Sam's Club|url=http://www3.samsclub.com/newsroom/AboutUs/ExecutiveTeam/216|access-date=July 22, 2013|work=Rosalind Brewer biography|publisher=Walmart|archive-date=September 8, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130908060223/http://www3.samsclub.com/newsroom/AboutUs/ExecutiveTeam/216|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2012, Brewer left Walmart and became the president and CEO of [[Sam's Club]], the membership-only retail warehouse clubs owned and operated by Walmart.<ref name="forbes">{{cite web|title=Rosalind Brewer|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/rosalind-brewer/|access-date=August 23, 2012|work=Worlds Most Powerful Women|publisher=Forbes}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/01/20/rosalind-brewer-sams-club_n_1219076.html |title=Rosalind Brewer, Named First Woman, black, CEO Of Sam's Club |work=The Huffington Post |date=January 20, 2012 |access-date=October 4, 2014 }}</ref> She focused on health and wellness by doubling the number of organic products offered at Sam's Clubs.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Most Powerful Women|url=https://fortune.com/most-powerful-women/|website=Fortune}}</ref> As CEO of [[Sam's Club|Sam's Club]], Brewer became the first black person to lead a Walmart division.<ref name=":1" /> She retired from her role at Sam's Club in 2017.<ref name=":1" />

=== Starbucks (2017-2021) ===
On February 1, 2017, Brewer was nominated for the [[Starbucks]] board of directors. On September 6, 2017, was named COO and group president.<ref>{{cite web|title=Starbucks Nominates Rosalind Brewer To Board of Directors|url=https://blavity.com/starbucks-nominates-rosalind-brewer-to-board-of-directors|access-date=February 17, 2017|website=Blavity.com|language=en |last1=F. |first1=Ebony }}</ref><ref name="greenstone">{{cite news|last=Greenstone|first=Scott|date=September 6, 2017|title=App-savvy new Starbucks COO is the first woman, black in company's highest echelon|newspaper=Seattle Times|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/business/starbucks/starbucks-names-brewer-as-no-2-exec/|access-date=September 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Starbucks Names Rosalind Brewer Group President and Chief Operating Officer|work=Starbucks Stories |url=https://stories.starbucks.com/press/2017/starbucks-names-rosalind-brewer-group-president-and-chief-operating-officer/}}</ref> Brewer was the second-highest-ranking executive at Starbucks after CEO [[Kevin Johnson (executive)|Kevin Johnson]] and the first black and the first woman to become the COO and group president of Starbucks.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|last=Connley|first=Courtney|date=September 14, 2017|title=3 things to know about Rosalind Brewer, Starbucks' first female and blackCOO|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/09/13/3-things-to-know-about-rosalind-brewer-starbucks-first-female-and-african-american-coo.html|access-date=March 24, 2021|website=CNBC|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Greenstone|first=Scott|title=App-savvy new Starbucks COO is the first woman, black person in company's highest echelon|date=September 6, 2017 |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/business/starbucks/starbucks-names-brewer-as-no-2-exec/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Wahba|first=Phil|title=Starbucks Has Recruited the Former CEO of Sam's Club to Run Its Operations|url=https://fortune.com/2017/09/06/starbucks-rosalind-brewer/}}</ref> She led businesses and operations in the United States, Canada, and Latin America.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Guynn|first=Jessica|title=Amazon names black Starbucks exec Rosalind Brewer to all-white board in 'barrier-breaking' appointment|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2019/02/04/amazon-names-starbucks-exec-rosalind-brewer-first-black-board-member/2769779002/|website=USA Today}}</ref>

=== Walgreens Boots Alliance (2021-2023)===
On March 15, 2021, Rosalind Brewer was appointed as the CEO of [[Walgreens Boots Alliance]]. Brewer became the only black woman to lead a [[Fortune 500|Fortune 500 company]] during that timeframe.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McGrath|first=Maggie|title=Breaking The 'Concrete' Ceiling: Roz Brewer To Become The S&P 500's Only Black Female CEO|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/maggiemcgrath/2021/01/28/breaking-the-concrete-ceiling-roz-brewer-to-be-the-sps-only-black-female-ceo/|access-date=March 24, 2021|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite news|last=Hirsch|first=Lauren|date=January 27, 2021|title=Walgreens picks a Starbucks executive to be its C.E.O.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/27/business/rosalind-brewer-walgreens.html|access-date=March 24, 2021|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

In 2023, Brewer's total compensation from Walgreens Boots Alliance was $14.1 million, or 407 times the median employee pay at Walgreens Boots Alliance for that year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Sarah |date=August 29, 2024 |title=Executive Excess 2024: The "Low Wage 100" corporations are enriching CEOs at the expense of workers and long-term investment |url=https://ips-dc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/executive_excess_2024_ips_report.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240829154904/https://ips-dc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/executive_excess_2024_ips_report.pdf |archive-date=August 29, 2024 |access-date=August 31, 2024 |website=[[Institute for Policy Studies]]}}</ref>

In September 2023, Brewer agreed to step down as CEO in September 2023 after being in the role for two years.<ref name="Kavilanz" /> Under Brewer's tenure as CEO, the company's stock declined 47%.<ref>{{cite web |date=September 1, 2023 |title=Walgreens CEO Brewer abruptly steps down after less than three years in role |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/walgreens-ceo-rosalind-brewer-steps-down-2023-09-01/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230920202355/https://www.reuters.com/business/walgreens-ceo-rosalind-brewer-steps-down-2023-09-01/ |archive-date=September 20, 2023 |access-date=August 31, 2024 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

=== Board memberships ===
Brewer was a member of the board of directors at [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] from 2019 to 2021.<ref name=":9" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Lystra|first=Tony|title=Roz Brewer will step down from Amazon's board before joining Walgreens|url=https://www.bizjournals.com/seattle/news/2021/02/02/roz-brewer-leaves-amazons-board-of-directors.html}}</ref> She was a director of [[Lockheed Martin]] from 2011 to 2017, and [[Molson Coors Brewing Company]] from 2006 to 2011.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":10" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Lockheed Martin Nominates Rosalind G. Brewer To Board Of Directors|url=https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2011-02-28-Lockheed-Martin-Nominates-Rosalind-G-Brewer-to-Board-of-Directors}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Molson Coors Appoints Rosalind G. Brewer to its Board of Directors|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24545/000118143106016014/rrd110034_12192.htm}}</ref>{{Excessive citations inline|date=September 2023}}

==Honors==
In 2020, ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'' ranked Brewer the 27th Most Powerful Woman in the World and ''[[Forbes]]'' ranked her 48th in their World's 100 Most Powerful Women.<ref name="profile" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web|title=Roz Brewer {{!}} 2020 Most Powerful Women|url=https://fortune.com/most-powerful-women/2020/roz-brewer/|access-date=March 24, 2021|website=Fortune|language=en}}</ref>

On September 15, 2015, ''Fortune'' included Brewer in its Most Powerful Woman rankings.<ref name=":8" /> ''[[Working Mother]]'' named her one of the Most Powerful Working Moms of 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Top 10 Most Powerful Moms of 2013|url=https://www.workingmother.com/content/top-10-most-powerful-moms-2013|access-date=March 24, 2021|website=Working Mother|language=en}}</ref>

In 2017, Brewer received the Spelman College Legacy of Leadership award.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rosalind Brewer- C'84|url=http://www.spelman.edu/about-us/office-of-the-president/board-of-trustees/rosalind-brewer|access-date=February 17, 2017|website=Spelman.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mason|first=Corinne|title=Reaching the Summit: Leadership Lessons from Successful Women – Rosalind Brewer|work=Summit Leadership Partners |url=https://www.summitleadership.com/rts-rosalind-brewer/}}</ref>

Brewer was selected for the inaugural 2021 ''Forbes'' 50 Over 50 list of entrepreneurs, leaders, scientists and creators over the age of 50.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gross |first1=Elana Lyn |last2=Voytko |first2=Lisette |last3=McGrath |first3=Maggie |url=https://www.forbes.com/50over50/ |title=The New Golden Age |work=[[Forbes]] |date=June 2, 2021 |accessdate=June 2, 2021 }}</ref> The same year, she was also inducted into the [[Michigan Women's Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rosalind "Roz" Brewer |url=https://miwf.org/timeline/rosalind-roz-brewer/ |access-date=January 26, 2024 |website=[[Michigan Women Forward]]}}</ref>

Brewer was named as one of ''[[USA Today]]'''s Women of the Year in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 28, 2022 |title=Meet USA TODAY's Women of the Year |url=https://www.usatoday.com/storytelling/grid/women-of-the-year-2022/ |access-date=September 5, 2022 |website=[[USA Today]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brewer is married to John Brewer, and they have two children.<ref name="profile" />

== Advocacy for diversity and inclusion ==
In 2015, as CEO of [[Sam's Club]], Brewer was interviewed on [[CNN]] by [[Poppy Harlow]]. During the interview, Brewer explained that diversity was a priority for her.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /> When speaking about the topic, she said, "I demand it of my team" and that, "Every now and then you have to nudge your partners. You have to speak up and speak out. And I try to use my platform for that. I try to set an example."<ref name=":7" /> Brewer described a specific incident when she was meeting with a supplier, and she recollected, "the entire other side of the table was all [[Caucasian race|Caucasian]] male. That was interesting."<ref name=":7" /> Brewer chose not to address the lack of diversity when meeting with the group, but said she was "going to make a call" to the supplier.<ref name=":7" /> In response to her comments, Brewer faced repercussions, as many individuals on social media called her "racist."<ref name=":6" />

In support of Brewer's statement, [[Doug McMillon]], [[Walmart]]'s president and [[Chief executive officer|CEO]], subsequently wrote in a statement, "For years, we've asked our suppliers to prioritize the talent and diversity of their sales teams calling on our company, Roz was simply trying to reiterate that we believe diverse and inclusive teams make for a stronger business. That's all there is to it and I support that important ideal."<ref name=":7">{{Cite news|last=O'Brien|first=Sara Ashley|title=Sam's Club CEO takes heat for diversity comments|work=CNN Business|url=https://money.cnn.com/2015/12/16/news/companies/rosalind-brewer-sams-club-diversity/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151219210849/http://money.cnn.com/2015/12/16/news/companies/rosalind-brewer-sams-club-diversity/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 19, 2015}}</ref>

Shortly after becoming the COO and group president of [[Starbucks]], the company was met with nationwide protests and negative publicity because of the arrest of two black men at a [[Philadelphia]] store location.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Gayle|first=Damien|title=Arrest of two black men at Starbucks for 'trespassing' sparks protests|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2018/apr/16/arrest-of-two-black-men-at-starbucks-for-trespassing-sparks-protests}}</ref> In response, Brewer and her team implemented policy changes and instituted [[racial bias]] training for employees in 8,000 stores.<ref>[https://www.forbes.com/profile/rosalind-brewer/#3dccda9a31d1] Forbes, "Power Women: Rosalind Brewer," 2018</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Reyes|first=Juliana Feliciano|title=Starbucks' CEO on racial training: We want to confront our biases 'and disrupt them'|work=The Philadelphia Inquirer|url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/news/starbucks-closed-racial-bias-training-may-29-philadelphia-20180529.html}}</ref>
